D-Phenylalanine is implicated in the interaction with two compounds, Agroastragaloside IV and 9-Isovaleroxy Balanophonin, both of which are targets of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. This indicates that D-Phenylalanine may act as a modulator or activator of the transporter, possibly through a mechanism involving the activation of the intermediate targets. The scores from the two paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with slight variations in the strength of the evidence. The mechanism likely involves the activation of the transporter by the interaction with these compounds, which may influence the transport of organic anions across cellular membranes. The evidence supports a plausible pathway, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the exact nature of the interaction.
